data.one_liner: Convenient value propagation and reactive observation for Flutter widgets.
data.what_it_does: Combines context_ref and context_watch to let you bind, propagate, and observe reactive values like Streams, Futures, Listenables, and Notifiers directly through the BuildContext with minimal boilerplate.
use_when: You want to share values down the widget tree without verbose InheritedWidgets.
You want to easily watch Listenables, Futures, or Streams inside widgets with automatic rebuilding.
You want a lightweight alternative to heavier state management frameworks.
avoid_when: You already rely heavily on Riverpod or Bloc for all state management and dependency injection.
Your project cannot use ContextPlus.root at the root of the application.
strengths: Drastically reduces boilerplate for watching streams, futures, and listenables.
Unifies context_ref and context_watch into a single package.
Supports multi-value observing via records up to 4 values.
Automatic cleanup and disposal of bound values tied to BuildContext lifecycle.
weaknesses: Requires wrapping your app in ContextPlus.root.
Relies on custom extension methods on BuildContext and Ref which might have a learning curve for new team members.
data.setup_notes: Wrap your root widget in ContextPlus.root(child: MaterialApp(...)) and optionally add the context_plus_lint plugin.
